items.title: Stratified sampling designs and the stratified total estimator
items.statement: Defines a finite-population partition, independent within-stratum SRSWOR samples, stratum sizes and finite-population variances, certainty strata, and the weighted total estimator.
items.strategy: Definition: specify the finite partition, integer sample-size domains, product design law, fixed-value convention, stratum means and variances only for noncertainty strata, and the weighted estimator.

items.title: Unbiasedness and variance of the stratified total estimator
items.statement: For independent within-stratum SRSWOR with every stratum sampled at least once, the weighted total estimator is design-unbiased and has variance equal to the sum of the noncertainty stratum SRSWOR variance contributions.
items.strategy: Direct: identify the stratified design as a finite design, express the estimator as the Horvitz–Thompson total for the stratum-specific inclusion probabilities, apply the SRSWOR variance formula within each stratum, and factor the product law to show cross-stratum covariances vanish.

items.title: Continuous fixed-size Neyman allocation minimizes stratified variance
items.statement: When all variable noncertainty strata have positive within-stratum variances, the uncapped continuous relaxation of the stratified variance at a fixed variable sample-size total is uniquely minimized by allocations proportional to stratum size times within-stratum standard deviation.
items.strategy: Direct: rewrite the variance objective as a sum of a_h squared over x_h plus a constant, then prove the finite Cauchy–Schwarz identity by a sum of pairwise squares and characterize its equality case.

items.title: Continuous cost-optimal stratified allocation
items.statement:
Use the notation of [[def-stratified-sampling-design-and-estimator]] and
[[thm-stratified-total-unbiasedness-and-variance]]. Let $J$ be a nonempty set
of variable noncertainty strata with $S_h>0$, and hold all other allocations
fixed. Assign each $h\in J$ a positive per-unit cost $c_h$. For a fixed
positive residual cost budget $C^\star$, the uncapped continuous relaxation
of the stratified variance expression, minimized over positive real
allocations $x_h>0$ for every $h\in J$ subject to
$\sum_{h\in J}c_hx_h=C^\star$, has the unique minimizer
$$x_h=C^\star\frac{N_hS_h/\sqrt{c_h}}{\sum_{k\in J}N_kS_k\sqrt{c_k}}\qquad(h\in J).$$
Thus $x_h\propto N_hS_h/\sqrt{c_h}$. As in the fixed-size result, this
continuous formula does not enforce integer, capacity, lower-bound, or
minimum-sample constraints.
items.strategy: Direct: rewrite the variance objective as a sum of a_h squared over x_h plus a constant, apply the finite pairwise-square identity with factors incorporating cost, and characterize the equality case under the cost constraint.

items.title: Proportional and disproportionate stratified allocations
items.statement: A two-stratum finite population compares proportional allocation (2,1) with disproportionate allocation (1,2), verifies both weighted estimators are unbiased, and computes their distinct design variances.
items.strategy: Verification: enumerate the fixed stratum means and variances, substitute both valid integer allocations into the estimator and variance formula, and check the weighted expectations and variance values.

items.title: A zero-variance stratum is outside the positive-variance allocation formula
items.statement: A finite population with one constant and one variable stratum shows that the unqualified Neyman proportionality assigns zero units to the constant stratum, violating the stratified design's positive sample-size requirement.
items.strategy: Verification: compute the stratum sizes, means and variances, evaluate the formal Neyman weights, identify the resulting zero allocation, and compute the variance for the smallest admissible positive allocation.

items.title: Continuous Neyman allocation may require constrained rounding
items.statement: A two-stratum example computes a fractional continuous Neyman allocation whose nearest-integer rounding assigns zero units to a stratum, so the continuous optimum does not itself specify an admissible stratified SRSWOR design.
items.strategy: Verification: construct finite strata with the stated sizes and variances, calculate the continuous allocation and nearest integers, check the design-domain violation, and evaluate the variance of an admissible minimum-sample allocation.
